Forbearance

/for-BAIR-uhns/ - the stress falls on BAIR · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Forbearance means patience and self-restraint when provoked.

Mrs. Idowu bore the trumpet practice next door with a forbearance that never once curdled into a complaint.

Worked Example

For eleven years the bookshop's loudest regular has mispronounced every author he buys, brought paperbacks back half-read with the spines cracked, and lectured the owner on stocking 'real literature.' She trades the damaged copies out, recommends his next book, and has never once told him what she thinks of his manners.

Forbearance is the exact word for the owner's restraint, because forbearance means patience and self-restraint when provoked — and the provocation is standing at her register, weekly. Patience alone is tested by delay; forbearance is tested by insult, and it holds anyway.

How Forbearance Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

restraint

restraint: holding yourself back in general; forbearance is restraint under provocation

patience

patience: calm through delay — no insult required

Antonyms

irritability

irritability: flaring at the smallest annoyance

vengefulness

vengefulness: answering every offense in kind

How Strong Is It? — politeness → patience → forbearance

politeness vs. forbearance

politeness vs. forbearance: Politeness is surface manners — you can be perfectly polite to a customer who has done nothing to try you.

patience vs. forbearance

patience vs. forbearance: Patience goes further than politeness — it stays calm through long delays — but patience is tested by time, while forbearance is tested by insult.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of forbearance.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — for-

Prefix — for-: against, holding off (Old English)

Root — bear

Root — bear: to carry, to endure

Suffix — -ance

Suffix — -ance: noun ending: the act of

Put it together

Put it together: For- (holding off) + bear (to carry, endure) + -ance = the act of bearing it while holding off. The old verb forbear meant to refrain — to carry the weight of an offense without setting it down on the offender — and forbearance is that carrying, made into a noun.

Use the root in a new word: unbearable

Use the root in a new word: unbearable: August in the attic apartment was unbearable — heat that could not be borne one hour more.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / admiring

Forbearance is the grown-up of the patience family: it holds steady while being provoked, and it chooses not to answer in kind. Its unit-mates work nearby — lenient softens the punishment an authority hands down, tactful takes the wounding words out of a sentence, accommodating rearranges plans. Forbearance simply absorbs the sting and stays kind.
